Hugging Face Daily Papers - 2026-08-15

32 papers today, with a strong cluster around world models, video generation, agent harnesses, AI scientists, long-term memory, and LLM reasoning efficiency.

Builds an interactive world model aimed at persistent memory, responsive interaction, and long-horizon generation.

3. DreamX-Phi 1.0: Action-Conditioned Video World Model for Robotic Manipulation
Presents an action-conditioned video world model that predicts robotic manipulation futures from frames, language, and robot actions.
https://t.co/sEy3yuA513

4. DarwinX: Evolving Agent Harnesses Through Natural Selection
Treats prompts, tools, skills, and control flow as evolvable agent harnesses that can improve through natural-selection-style loops.
https://t.co/CQ2lPLW8y6

5. Intern-S2-Preview: Scientific Agentic Foundation Model
Proposes an agentic foundation model for scientific discovery across heterogeneous scientific evidence, tools, and modalities.
https://t.co/3X2I4wB3kz

6. How Can Rhetoric Reward-Hack AI Reviewers? Dissecting Rhetorical Sensitivity in AI-Based Peer Review
Analyzes how rhetorical choices can manipulate AI-based peer review, exposing a subtle reward-hacking risk in scientific evaluation.
https://t.co/NsKbZFBHAJ

7. AutoDesign: Meta-Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Design
Frames multimodal design generation as a long-horizon agentic process and optimizes the agent harness behind it.
https://t.co/zCvR04xZgW

8. PlayWorld: Benchmarking World Models with Agent Players over Long-Horizon Objectives
Benchmarks video world models by letting agent players pursue long-horizon objectives inside generated environments.
https://t.co/3j4YNA2nAK

9. Spatial Memory Agent: Experience-Grounded Procedure Memory for Spatial Intelligence
Adds experience-grounded procedural memory to improve spatial reasoning for embodied agents and multimodal assistants.
https://t.co/dIg5QqZ6aY

10. Massive Activations in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models: Pre-Attention Spikes and Inter-Spike Plateaus
Provides a first systematic study of massive activations in hybrid linear-attention LLMs, identifying pre-attention spikes and inter-spike plateaus.
https://t.co/6Le0j7uZTU

11. UniSwap: Streaming Audio-Visual Identity Swapping for Talking Videos
Enables streaming identity swapping in talking videos by jointly transferring appearance and voice while preserving motion and scene context.
https://t.co/x5VMUjUXGd

12. LiveAnimate: Stable Long-Form Streaming Human Animation in Real-Time
Targets real-time, long-form, pose-driven human animation from a single reference image with improved streaming stability.
https://t.co/Y37SOzTb8E

13. Full-bandwidth transformer
Rethinks autoregressive transformer computation across token and depth axes to improve bandwidth and inference dynamics.
https://t.co/6SS6fXHnIk

14. H2R-Bench: Benchmarking Human-to-Robot Manipulation Video Generation in World Models
Introduces a benchmark for using human manipulation videos to evaluate robot-oriented world-model video generation.
https://t.co/5f76IgdFSo

15. An AI4AI Framework for Visual Token Pruning
Uses AI-driven design to prune visual tokens and reduce multimodal LLM inference cost while preserving performance.
https://t.co/lTYYcFzNGc

16. OmniScientist: An Omni-Modal Omni-Discipline AI Scientist
Builds toward an omni-modal, cross-discipline AI scientist that automates broader research workflows.
https://t.co/yZ24oEwpgx

17. AVA-Encoder: Towards Agent-Native Video Representation Learning
Learns video representations tailored for creative agents that need to understand and generate cinematic-quality video.
https://t.co/IMgK5lTlNE

18. Thought-Level Beam Search for Reasoning
Improves test-time reasoning efficiency by searching over thought-level candidates rather than relying only on expensive linear sampling.
https://t.co/rruNmBRJ2w

19. Context-Matched Distillation: Teacher Causality for Autoregressive Video Distillation
Accelerates interactive autoregressive video generation through distillation that better matches causal teacher context.
https://t.co/22lNCWON3d

20. SKILLER: Language-Level Reinforcement Learning for Reusable Skill Extraction in Small Language Models
Uses language-level reinforcement learning to extract reusable procedural skills for small language-model agents.
https://t.co/hXz8UyWEwp

21. Maglev: Sliding Recurrent Memory
Introduces a recurrent Transformer memory architecture that generalizes sliding-window attention with fixed-size memory.
https://t.co/TCTDaKPtrl

22. LycheeMemory V2: Efficient Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents via Semantic Segment-Level Consolidation
Improves long-term memory for LLM agents by consolidating interaction history into semantic segments instead of eager compression.
https://t.co/7GrLAAjrjZ

23. Hybrid-Policy Self-Editing for Composable Unstructured Knowledge Editing
Combines policy strategies for self-editing LLM knowledge over composable, unstructured updates.
https://t.co/8GPxy4kxbv

24. Are You Sure You're Sure? On the Impact of Instruction Tuning on Confidence and Lexical Diversity
Studies how instruction tuning affects model confidence and lexical diversity, probing overconfidence and verbosity patterns.
https://t.co/tuUJTrOyqt

25. Knowing When to Quit: Diagnosing and Training LLMs to Abort Futile Reasoning
Diagnoses wasteful reasoning on beyond-capability tasks and trains LLMs to abort when continued reasoning is futile.
https://t.co/3QvXTeyaDV

26. Specification-first convergence with an AI coding agent: a case study of dismantling a core architectural invariant across 189 files in a 717k-line codebase with no test oracle and no human code review
Reports a large-scale AI coding-agent refactor guided by specifications in a 717k-line codebase without a conventional test oracle.
https://t.co/IYXOwWBkQA

https://t.co/RbEdYTbOV5

28. TailBooster: A Dual-Layer Generative Framework for Extreme Value Augmentation with Operational Validity Enforcement
Generates operationally valid extreme-value examples for air-transport scenarios such as severe delays and abnormal air times.
https://t.co/dQYxhjC2NV

29. PixSDS: Why Latent SDS Makes Noisy Pixels
Investigates why latent score distillation sampling can produce noisy pixels and proposes a clearer path for improving 3D generation quality.
https://t.co/HDceBWVy4r

30. CW-BASS v2: Saturation-Aware Pseudo-Label Selection for Semi-Supervised Segmentation under Foundation-Model Teachers
Improves semi-supervised segmentation by selecting pseudo-labels with saturation awareness under foundation-model teachers.
https://t.co/UG8wUrzwx8

https://t.co/LAB8BzTX8A

Targets gender-bias mitigation in English-to-Romanian machine translation, a practical fairness problem in multilingual NLP.

Prompt for AI video generation (Runway / Kling / Luma / Hailuo / etc.)

A vertical 9:16 cinematic AI art video, 10 seconds long, smooth continuous morphing transformation of a hyper-detailed surreal fashion portrait of a beautiful woman.

The face is always split vertically down the middle: left side porcelain-white skin with icy blue eyes and glossy red lips, right side deep matte black skin with glowing red eyes and metallic silver lips. High-fashion editorial beauty, sharp features, intense gaze looking straight at camera.

Throughout the video the face constantly shatters and recomposes with floating geometric fragments: sharp white and black triangular shards, cracked porcelain pieces, paper-like geometric planes, and bold red triangular cutouts that slide across the eyes, cheek, and lips. Large delicate white flowers (cosmos/peony style) bloom and dissolve over the head and face. A small delicate white bird occasionally appears perched on a flower or flying across the composition. Soft smoke and abstract black-and-white fabric shapes swirl around.

Sequence of elegant morphs:
- Start with cracked geometric glasses and floating white cubes
- Transition into flower-crowned face with bird and shattered glass
- Minimalist black/white face with pure white triangles
- Bold red geometric cutouts over the mouth and cheek
- Full floral headdress with bird and red triangle accent
- Abstract fragmented flower-covered face with single red eye
- Cracked flower-over-face composition with flying bird
- Dualistic face with black/white flowers and red diagonal slash
- Final intense geometric shatter with red triangles and floating petals

Ultra-detailed skin texture, dramatic high-contrast lighting, dark abstract background, cinematic depth of field, smooth slow morphing animation, dreamlike and elegant, no text, no watermark.

**Music / audio:**
Dark elegant ethereal ambient track — soft melancholic piano, subtle low strings, atmospheric pads, and delicate glassy textures. Mysterious, sophisticated, slightly haunting mood that perfectly matches the black/white dualism and red accents. Soft dynamic swells that follow the morphing transformations. No vocals, high-quality stereo, cinematic and intimate.

Tarun on how AI training evolved from pre-training to self generating harnesses and why data costs are catching up to compute

"Let's take a tiny history lesson. In 2023, with stable diffusion and GPT-3, it was just bigger is better, pre-training. Then in 2024 it was directed RL, how you feed the data after training, this in context learning type of stuff, which got you another order of magnitude performance increase across a lot of evals and practical use cases"

"Then the harness thing was, if you customize how you do the RL for different applications, you get even better performance versus a generic RL environment. And the current meta-harness, the generic can answer anything, Claude Code or Codex type of thing, which arguably is what killed Cursor and why I'd argue they ended up doing the acquisition, that can figure out which environment to use just in time"

"The problem with this environment stuff from a data consumption perspective is you now have to pay a lot more for annotated data to customize the different environments. That's why people have been talking about data cost coming close to matching compute cost for training, because you need much more annotated data for each specific task domain"

"The belief is that once one of these things is good enough, instead of having to get data this way and generating synthetic data via RL, the model can generate the harness in real time"

The same problem resurfaces in LLM evaluation. A benchmark score gets read as a direct measure of capability, but it is an aggregate over items that are not interchangeable instruments.

Zhou et al. fit an item response model to 41,871 items across 11 benchmarks and estimated difficulty, discriminability, guessing rate, and feasibility for each one. The aggregate conceals how uneven these are. Some items have discriminability near zero and separate nothing. Some carry guessing rates above 0.75, which the authors read as a contamination signal. Estimated item difficulty rarely exceeds 1.0 while the strongest models sit above 3.0. TheoremQA averages 0.50 on feasibility, so many of its questions cannot be answered from what they supply.

The cost is measurable. Among the stronger models, 1,000 items selected for Fisher information reproduced the human-preference ranking at Kendall's τ of 0.90, while the full pooled set managed 0.24. More items made the ranking worse. The question is not who scored higher on accuracy, but who was separated by items capable of separating anything. 8/9
